anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

pass_a_gloss: And these things are enough said about the bare name, for us to be taught what is signified from the naming of phas and to be built up, not rashly applying ourselves to those attempting the things said in Hebrew and not without first having known the Hebrew interpretation. We shall come already to the examination of the very sayings, the pascha signifying crossing.
pass_b_english: And this is enough said about the name itself, taken simply — enough for us to be taught what is signified by the name phas, and enough for us to be built up: not to throw ourselves rashly at the things said in Hebrew, attempting them without first having come to know the Hebrew interpretation. We shall now come to the examination of the very words. The Passover signifies crossing.
source_text: Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν [ἱ]κανὰ περὶ αὐτῆς ψιλῆς τῆς [ὀν]ομασίας εἴρηται εἰς τὸ δ[ιδ]αχθῆναι ἡμᾶς τί τὸ σημ[αιν]όμενον ἐκ τῆς τοῦ φας ὀνομασί[α]ς καὶ εἰς τὸ οἰκοδομηθῆναι, μὴ προπετῶς τοῖς ἑβραϊκῶς εἰ[ρη]μένοις ἐπιχειροῦσι ἐπιβά[λλε]ιν καὶ μὴ οὐχὶ πρότερον [τὴ]ν ἑρμήνειαν τὴν ἑβραϊ[κ]ὴν ἐπεγνωκόσι[ν], ἐλευσόμ[εθα δ]ὲ κ[αὶ] ἐπ’ αὐτῶν ἤδη τῶν [ῥη]τ[ῶν τὴ]ν ἐξέτ[α]σιν, διάβ[ασι]ν ση[μα]ίνοντος τοῦ πάσχ[α].
